title: original a100 pilot
question: What are peak CUDA allocation and training throughput on original AirfRANS meshes?
hypothesis: A full A100 can train the default Transolver with 32000 sampled nodes per step.
protocol: Full-task training cases only, seed 0, batch one, float32, Adam and one-cycle schedule. Time synchronised steps after warm-up. Use a bounded training-case subset for a hardware pilot.
decision_rule: Record finite training steps, peak allocated and reserved bytes, and steady-state steps per second before proposing a full-run budget.
budget: One full A100, one job, at most 60 wall minutes. No CFD.
